title.value: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime

logline: A murdered Tokyo salaryman reincarnates as a slime in a fantasy world, absorbs the powers of everything he touches, and builds a monster nation through diplomacy and overwhelming competence.

renewal.note: Season 3 concluded in September 2024. Season 4 is scheduled to premiere April 3, 2026, with a planned 5-cour run. A theatrical film - Tears of the Azure Sea - released in 2026.

bollymeter.basis: The single Rotten Tomatoes critic review gave it 6/10 noting the RPG elements and protagonist progression are intriguing. IMDb series rating tracks in the high sevens. Reception positions it as a warm, well-executed isekai that subverts power fantasy conventions through a protagonist more interested in governance than combat.

pull_quotes.text: The RPG elements, the main concept, and the way the protagonist progresses are rather intriguing.
pull_quotes.source: Asian Movie Pulse via Rotten Tomatoes

seasons.review_body: Eight Bit's adaptation of Fuse's light novel debuted in October 2018, standing out in a crowded isekai season by making its protagonist an earnest builder rather than a combat fetishist. Satoru Mikami, reincarnated as a slime named Rimuru, absorbs the abilities of everything he encounters and consistently uses them to negotiate peace and construct systems rather than simply dominate. The first season establishes the Jura Tempest Federation, introduces the goblin and wolf tribes, and handles its worldbuilding at a measured, confident pace. The tonal warmth becomes its key differentiator, as the fantasy world feels genuinely habitable and Rimuru's cooperative approach creates stakes without leaning on constant mortal peril. The series comes across as solid and dependable, a well-made isekai with character that compounds across seasons.

episode_reviews.title: The Storm Dragon, Veldora
episode_reviews.review_body: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime Season 1 Episode 1 'The Storm Dragon, Veldora' aired October 2, 2018 on Tokyo MX as the premiere of the 24-episode first season. IMDb scored the series 7.9; Asian Movie Pulse via Rotten Tomatoes noted 'the RPG elements, the main concept, and the way the protagonist progresses are rather intriguing.' Eight Bit's premiere handles the isekai premise with unusual efficiency: Satoru Mikami is murdered, reincarnates as a slime, meets the sealed Storm Dragon Veldora, and names himself Rimuru - all within one episode that never feels compressed. The visual warmth Eight Bit establishes here sustains the entire series. The tone is immediately differentiated from grimmer isekai entries: cooperative, curious, governance-oriented rather than combat-focused. The pact between Rimuru and Veldora - the slime names the dragon, the dragon grants a skill set - is the series' founding transaction, sealed in ten minutes.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere handles the isekai premise with uncommon efficiency: Satoru is murdered, reincarnates as a slime, meets the sealed Storm Dragon Veldora, and names himself Rimuru - all in one episode that never feels rushed. Eight Bit establishes a visual warmth that the series sustains. The tone is immediately, reassuringly different from the genre's grimmer entries.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Rimuru and Veldora's pact - the slime names the dragon, the dragon grants a skill set, and the show's central friendship is sealed in ten minutes.

episode_reviews.title: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
episode_reviews.review_body: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime Season 1 Episode 24 'That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime' aired March 19, 2019 on Tokyo MX as the season finale of the 24-episode first season. IMDb scored the series 7.9; Asian Movie Pulse noted the protagonist's intriguing progression. The finale consolidates Rimuru's nation-building achievement across the first season and closes the founding arc with the Jura Tempest Federation's first formal gathering: economic and political consequence rendered as warmth rather than grimness. Eight Bit's production sustains the visual identity established in Episode 1. The episode functions both as conclusion and invitation - the slime who chose diplomacy over domination has built something worth protecting, and the season ends by showing, rather than declaring, what that means.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale consolidates Rimuru's nation-building achievement and closes the first major arc on a note that functions as both conclusion and invitation. The episode demonstrates what the series does better than most isekai: economic and political consequence rendered as warmth rather than grimness.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The Jura Tempest Federation's first formal gathering - the show's thesis on cooperative world-building made visible.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 escalates the political and military stakes significantly and includes the Megiddo episode (IMDb 9.4) - the single highest-rated episode in the series. The split-cour format (January-March and July-September 2021) maintained audience engagement across a mid-year gap.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 aired in two cours across 2021 and marked a tonal shift: Rimuru's nation faces genuine military threat from the Kingdom of Falmuth, and the show's normally cheerful diplomatic fantasy pivots into its darkest material. The Octagram arc introduces the demon lords and significantly expands the world's political geography. The Megiddo episode - Rimuru's response to the Falmuth invasion - became the series' most-discussed individual episode, rated 9.4 on IMDb, and demonstrated that the show's power fantasy underpinning had genuine emotional weight when the protagonist was cornered. Critics and audiences sustained enthusiasm, with the split-cour format generating anticipation rather than fatigue. Season 2 is where the Tempest storyline becomes a genuine long-form narrative rather than episodic world-building.
seasons.season_over_season: The political stakes arrive in force - darker tone, higher consequences, and the series' single best episode in the Megiddo arc.

episode_reviews.title: Megiddo
episode_reviews.review_body: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime Season 2 Episode 46 'Megiddo' aired August 17, 2021 on Tokyo MX as part of the second cour of Season 2. IMDb scored the episode 9.4 - the highest-rated episode in the franchise. Season 2 built toward this confrontation with the Kingdom of Falmuth across 24 episodes, and Megiddo is where the franchise's accumulated power fantasy finds its most earned expression. Eight Bit deploys Rimuru's full ability set in a sequence that lands with both technical polish and emotional weight that the series' lighter earlier episodes do not prepare the audience for. The tonal shift from diplomatic fantasy to military response had been developing across the season's second half; Megiddo is where it arrives. Rimuru's response to the invasion is presented as devastating rather than triumphant, which is the episode's crucial distinction from standard power-fantasy resolution.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The episode that most often gets mentioned first when justifying the franchise shows Rimuru responding to the Falmuth invasion by deploying his accumulated abilities at full scale. The sequence lands with both technical polish and emotional weight that the show's lighter earlier episodes do not prepare for. The power fantasy reaches its most earned form here.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Rimuru's Megiddo attack - the moment the show revealed what it had been building toward all along.

bollymeter.basis: Season 3 covers the Demon Lord Awakening and Labyrinth arcs, expanding the world's upper power tier. Reception among ongoing viewers remained warm, though the density of political intrigue and large cast prompted some audience commentary on accessibility for newer viewers.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 ran from April to September 2024, chronicling Rimuru's rise among the Octagram demon lords and the Labyrinth's emergence as a new geopolitical institution. Eight Bit sustained the production quality and the show's warm ensemble dynamic, but Season 3's political density, with an expanding roster of named demon lords, layered regional power conflicts, and nested faction agendas, made it the most demanding entry point in the franchise. The payoff for long-seeded relationships and alliances built across earlier seasons comes through in a satisfying way. The season also sustains the genre's dependable rhythm without the dramatic creative spikes seen in Season 2's Megiddo.
seasons.season_over_season: Expands the world's upper tier considerably - rewards accumulated investment but is the densest entry yet for newcomers.
